speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe how the difficulty walking has progressed and if you notice any weakness or numbness in your legs. When did your speech difficulties and urinary incontinence first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the urinary incontinence been associated with a loss of sensation in your legs or saddle area, and do you experience any tingling or numbness?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, MRI of the spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Clear appearance, 0-5 WBC/HPF, 0-2 RBC/HPF, Negative Nitrites, Negative Leukocyte Esterase; MRI Spinal Cord: Findings consistent with MRI Brain (Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes). Note: The patient reports urinary incontinence, but the provided data does not include specific sensory exam results regarding loss of sensation in the legs or saddle area, nor specific MRI findings isolated to the spinal cord beyond the general neurodegenerative changes noted in the brain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) with pyramidal, cerebellar, and autonomic involvement.
